purpose: What is the longest piece that cuts both ribbons without waste?
meaning: The greatest common divisor of two positive integers is the largest positive integer dividing both. Repeat division with remainder until the remainder is zero. The final nonzero divisor is the greatest common divisor of the two positive lengths.

definition.setting: Cut two ribbons of integer lengths a and b centimetres into equal whole-centimetre pieces with no waste. Euclidean division finds the longest permitted piece.

conditions: Both lengths are positive integers from 1 to 60 cm. The gcd is the longest common whole-centimetre length, not the largest number of pieces or a measurement of arbitrary real lengths.

properties.claim: A Euclidean replacement preserves common divisors.
properties.conditions: Both lengths are positive integers from 1 to 60 cm. The gcd is the longest common whole-centimetre length, not the largest number of pieces or a measurement of arbitrary real lengths.
properties.derivation: From a=qb+r, any common divisor of a,b divides r=a−qb; any common divisor of b,r divides a=qb+r.
